commits.messageBody:
Keep the existing signed-int block representation and fail through FATAL
before an unrepresentable request changes allocation state. Derive the
bound from header/guard layout and region rounding, including the 30-bit
requested-size field where enabled. Split large preallocation into bounded
regions and check MiB arithmetic before addition.

Native VS2013 Debug/Release, Win32/x64: tracked and untracked boundary
probes each 21/21; tracked real-allocator regression 2568/2568; small-region
preallocation 12/12. Rejection uses actual FatalException support and keeps
the old realloc payload. The region probe lowers only its diagnostic
region maximum to exercise the loop with 3 MiB, not giant reservations.

Aggregate statistics above 4 GiB and tracked realloc(NULL) remain separate.
Evidence: review/client-x64-evidence, allocator-size-audit.md packet.
commits.messageHeadline: memory: check allocation and region sizes before narrowing

commits.messageBody:
Untracked x64 allocations could be rounded to 48 bytes even though FreeBlock
occupies 56 bytes (64 after allocator alignment). The old subdivision test
could also leave a 48-byte remainder. Require both allocated blocks and split
remainders to fit the aligned free-list node; retain the existing split rule.
Win32's existing 32-byte minimum already satisfies the same invariant.

Native VS2013 candidate validation passes 1622/1622 checks in each of Release
and Debug on Win32 and x64: sizes 0..512, real allocate/free/reallocate cycles,
payload preservation, block-chain invariants and bounded region-edge sizes.
Win32 small-size calculations are checked against the previous expression.
The tests use the untracked product layout; this is not a whole-client heap
or tracked-allocation acceptance claim.
commits.messageHeadline: memory: keep x64 blocks large enough for their free-list representation
